decision: routed to figure-it-out, not Feature or Autonomous-run alone
why: seven distinct test methodologies across a financial ledger is an ambitious multi-part change, which poteto-mode routes to figure-it-out even when a narrower playbook fits
evidence: .claude/skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md

decision: captured the pre-change baseline before writing any test
why: the harness has to read as old value vs new value, so the run can prove it moved something
evidence: npm test exit 0, 148 vitest tests in 8 files, 8 SQL ledger stages, 35 SQL assertions

decision: measured baseline mutation score before adding tests
why: mutation score is the only falsifiable measure of whether the new tests actually catch defects
evidence: reports/mutation/mutation.json, 814 mutants, 112 killed

decision: each database-backed suite gets its own database cloned from a template, instead of sharing one and locking
why: concurrent suites writing one database is shared mutable state; eliminating the sharing beats serialising access to it
evidence: measured CREATE DATABASE TEMPLATE at 83ms for the 21-table schema
result: per-suite isolation is cheap enough to use everywhere

decision: built the shared harness first, before any of the seven suites
why: every database-backed technique needs the same three things: its own database, a typed way to call ledger.post, and one oracle for the books
evidence: tests/support/database.ts, tests/support/global-setup.ts

decision: proved the oracle fails on a deliberately corrupted ledger, not just that it passes on a clean one
why: an oracle only ever seen passing is indistinguishable from one that always returns healthy
evidence: tests/support/harness.test.ts, the corrupted-leg case
result: oracle reports unbalancedEntries > 0 on a broken book

decision: found that ledger.post records actor_user_id and never reads it
why: maker-checker separation is the compliance rule the brief names, and the database does not enforce it
evidence: db/post.sql, app.lifecycle_edge.actor_role is written by the seed and read by nothing
result: open, to be pinned by a decision table

decision: found five uncovered races, including a lock-order inversion between settle_maturity and accept_bid
why: the existing concurrency test covers one race out of six and is timing-dependent
evidence: tests/ledger/concurrency.sh covers only the contended accept
result: open, to be covered by unit 7

decision: seven techniques become seven units, six of them delegated in parallel
why: the six write disjoint files against disjoint databases, so there is no seam to serialise; mutation testing runs last because it measures the other six
evidence: tests/support/CONTRACT.md is the shared recipe all six read

decision: made mutation score the predicate for the whole run, not a seventh deliverable
why: a suite can grow by hundreds of green assertions without catching one more defect; the mutation score is the only number that says otherwise
evidence: baseline 13.76 percent recorded before any suite was written

decision: told delegates never to run git and to own exactly two paths each
why: six agents committing into one working tree is the same shared-state problem as one database, and file ownership removes it without needing six worktrees
evidence: tests/support/CONTRACT.md rules 5 and 6

decision: told delegates to keep a failing test and write it up rather than change src or db
why: the brief asked for tests; a suite that edits the system under test to go green proves nothing
evidence: tests/support/CONTRACT.md rule 4, it.fails plus a findings file

decision: found and fixed my own harness dropping other runs' databases
why: global-setup swept every adata_x_ database at startup and every template at teardown, which would delete the six parallel suites' databases mid-test
evidence: commit 838cc7d, tests/support/global-setup.ts

decision: reproduced all three property-test defects myself instead of trusting the delegate's report
why: a delegate's summary is not evidence; the artifact is
evidence: ran an independent throwaway suite against src/core, 4 of 4 assertions passed, then deleted it

decision: formatUnits emits a string parseUnits refuses, from 1000 display units up
why: the module's own formatter and its own parser disagree, so a formatted figure cannot be fed back in
evidence: src/core/money.ts, counterexample 10000000n formats to 1,000.0000

decision: parseFilter throws on ?smin=1e305 although it documents never rejecting
why: a mangled marketplace URL becomes a server error rather than an unfiltered list
evidence: src/core/market.ts units() guards isFinite before the multiply that overflows

decision: allocateProRata over-allocates when a weight is negative
why: its guard tests the sum of weights, which is narrower than the postcondition it documents
evidence: src/core/money.ts, total 1n weights [-4n,10n,-1n] returns parts summing to 2n
result: confirmed, latent, unreachable from any screen today

decision: top_up with no amountBase is accepted and returns a confirmed receipt with zero legs
why: reproduced it myself against the running database, not from the delegate's report
evidence: ledger.post returned legs [] status confirmed with a txHash; journal_entry row is chain_status confirmed
result: VERIFIED, the worst finding so far

decision: noted the ledger oracle cannot catch the zero-leg top_up
why: an entry with no legs balances trivially, so conservation stays true while the receipt lies
evidence: ledgerHealth returns HEALTHY on that entry
result: why a partition table found it and the oracle did not

decision: money.ts mutation score moved from 7.97 to 17.13 percent once the new suites were in scope
why: the mutation config only included src tests, so it could not see tests/techniques and the score would not have moved at all
evidence: vitest.unit.config.mts now includes tests/techniques, 43 killed against 20 at baseline

decision: a bid below the listing's min_price_base is accepted and settles
why: verified myself: min_price_base appears only in insert column lists and a check on the listing row, never compared to a bid price on any acceptance path
evidence: db/post.sql lines 477 and 531, db/schema.sql line 391

decision: settle_maturity never reads receipt_status, so a rejected payable redeems
why: verified myself: the settle_maturity branch, db/post.sql 667 to 740, contains no reference to receipt_status at all
evidence: its four guards are fundingCode, already settled, maturity and anchor wallet

decision: maker-checker is enforced on no write path in either layer
why: lifecycle.ts attempt() is called from the approvals page only to decide whether to draw a button; the server action posts approve with no role argument
evidence: src/app/adata/approvals/page.tsx 124-127 against src/app/actions.ts
result: VERIFIED, corrects my earlier claim that attempt() was called only from its own test

decision: ABBA deadlock between settle_maturity and accept_bid, confirmed against the source
why: db/post.sql lines 7-13 state the lock order is payable then series then listing, and accept_bid takes listing at 589 before payable at 636 while settle_maturity takes payable at 676 before listings at 698
evidence: both deadlock victims covered, 40P01 either way, books HEALTHY in both
result: VERIFIED, the code contradicts its own stated contract

decision: redeeming one member of a listed series strands its siblings' escrow
why: settle_maturity cancels the whole series listing but unwinds escrow only for the settled asset, so the deferred escrow equality fails at COMMIT with ADA04
evidence: db/post.sql 693-699 against the asset filter at 704
result: reported by the suite, deferred trigger fires at COMMIT not at the statement

decision: mutation score moved 13.76 to 22.60 percent, and the score is now a gate at 22
why: a suite can grow by hundreds of green assertions without catching one more defect, so the run needed a number that says otherwise
evidence: stryker.config.json thresholds.break, scripts/test.sh mutation stage

decision: proved Stryker's 0.00 percent for fx.ts is a measurement failure, not a coverage hole
why: when something looks wrong, suspect the observation method before the system
evidence: hand-planted a mutation in src/core/fx.ts, three tests failed, then restored the file
result: artifact documented, fx.ts kept in scope rather than excluded

decision: the select-or-insert NULL race I briefed does not reproduce
why: six simultaneous first-ever top-ups to a brand-new wallet all succeeded onto one account row; ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING waits on the in-progress tuple and each statement inside a VOLATILE function takes a fresh snapshot
evidence: tests/techniques/findings/concurrency-faults.md, measured not inferred

decision: the unlocked holder read in settle_maturity is not exploitable today
why: the loop is covered by the app.payable row lock taken forty lines above it, not by anything the loop does; pg_blocking_pids shows the settlement queued behind a session holding only that row
evidence: recorded as a latent hazard with the conditions that would reintroduce it
result: safe, but accidentally so and documented nowhere

decision: redeeming one member of a listed series is refused outright in autocommit
why: settle_maturity cancels the whole series listing but unwinds escrow for the settled asset only, so the deferred escrow equality fails at COMMIT
evidence: db/post.sql 693-699 against the filter at 704; members share a maturity date so every listed series lot hits this on the first member

decision: supersedes my claim that the mutation score is the predicate for the whole run
why: it mutates src/core only, and four of the seven suites import nothing from src/core; they test db/post.sql, which no mutation tool here touches
evidence: import counts: properties 5, equivalence-boundary 5, decision-tables 1, the other three 0
